messages:
jordan: Heads-up: Security just flagged a CVE in musl used by our slim base images. We need a coordinated rebuild + signing+audit flow. Timeline: start rebuild tonight in staging, promote tomorrow if canaries pass. Need RBAC for extra security scans and temporary KMS access for re-signing. Who can own temporary policy?

nina: I can own the RBAC window. Proposal: create a short-lived IAM binding that grants ci-scan-sa the roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier on the signing key and roles/storage.objectViewer on the log bucket, with a condition limiting to the rebuild job name and expiry timestamp. We'll remove it automatically via the prow job.

tas: Agree. Also request we enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for KMS immediately so sign ops are recorded. Devs: do not attempt manual key export or copy. Use cosign + KMS only.

ops-oncall: Reminder: in previous rotation we lacked cross-project audit filter. Route KMS DATA_ACCESS to a dedicated log sink in project-sec-logs and apply retention_lock 395 days. Ops will create the sink and lock.

jordan: Nina, can you paste the minimal IAM binding snippet here so security review can sign-off? Also need a checklist for: build, scan, rebase, sign, publish, canary.

nina: Snippet (minimal):

```yaml
- role: roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier
  members:
    - serviceAccount:ci-scan@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  condition:
    title: "rebuild-window"
    expression: "request.time < timestamp('2026-04-01T04:00:00Z') && resource.name.startsWith('projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/signing')"
```

Also add storage.objectViewer on projects/redwood-prod/buckets/signing-logs with the same condition.

paul: Quick note on signing: we'll use cosign with KMS key versions and attestations. CI will create an attestation with predicate containing git_sha, docker_manifest_digest, builder_sa, vuln_scan_hash. Consumers can validate via cosign verify-attestation.

sec-bot: auto: Scanner found musl-1.2.3 CVE-2026-1234 in base-slim:v2026-03 (high). Affected runtime layers derived from that base. Recommended action: rebuild base from upstream patched musl or switch to glibc-based minimal until upstream releases fix.

jordan: For the rebuild flow: 1) fork current base Dockerfile, update musl to patched version (or pin to upstream commit), 2) build in staging, 3) run full vuln scan + runtime sec-assertions (non-root, seccomp, capabilities), 4) sign with KMS-backed cosign and push to staging registry, 5) run 5% prod canary on dedicated nodes, 6) roll to 100% if no regressions.

tas: On the sec-assertions: we'll run container-cap-check, seccomp-smoke, and a quick e2e to exercise typical request paths. I'll add a gating job in CI that fails the build if unexpected capabilities are present.

ops-oncall: Canary plan: traffic-split via service mesh at 5% for 2 hours, metrics and error budget checks. If error rate > 0.5% or latency regress > 30% revert via traffic rollback and revoke signing key version just in case.

paul: For provenance, we'll log an immutable row to artifact_catalog dataset in BigQuery with columns: artifact_digest, builder_sa, git_sha, base_image_digest, signing_key_version, build_ts, scan_summary_hash. That lets IR teams quickly find impacted builds.

jordan: Good. Two operational asks: (1) security needs a short drill in staging to simulate key compromise and rotation — ops, can you schedule? (2) Nina, ensure the IAM condition uses a hard expiry and minimal scope.

nina: Will do both. I'll create the ephemeral-binding job that tears itself down and paste the full YAML after review.

sec-bot: auto: Created ticket SEC-7400: musl base rebuild + ephemeral RBAC + KMS DATA_ACCESS + canary plan.

ops-oncall: Scheduling drill for tomorrow 2200Z in staging. Will invite oncall rotation and platform reviewers.

jordan: Thanks everyone. After the staging run I'll open a post-build thread with artifacts and the final sign-off. Keeping this channel updated if anything changes.
